title: Draw a tie that runs both ways as one line with no arrowhead.
rule: Use symmetrical links, a reference form, where a tie means the same from either end, such as two agencies that share board members: draw each tie as one plain line with no arrowhead, as thick as its strength where it has one. Where a tie runs one way, give it an arrowhead (Rule 14.104), and where the two ways carry different amounts, draw two arcs, each with its own arrowhead and width.
use_when: The reader asks who is tied to whom, and each tie means the same from either end.

use_instead.when: Ties that run one way, with amounts
Flows both ways among a few groups

text: An arrowhead claims a direction, and on a shared tie it would invent one. One plain line says the tie is shared.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: No kit form: draw each tie with K.parts.link and no arrow, its width the tie’s strength.
sketch_alt: Four nodes joined by plain lines with no arrowheads, each line as thick as the tie it draws.
